I am an old man of 72 years, farming here in the North West for many seasons. This small plot of 0.25 hectares near the compound I plant with beans mixed with other crops — that is how we do it, intercropping helps the soil and gives us more from small land. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer for the legumes because beans fix their own nitrogen in the soil, but I will put some manure from my goats and sheep. I use the seed I saved from last harvest, and with my age my sons and grandchildren help me with the work, though for weeding time I may call one or two young men from the village to help.
